title: Stop the misuse of short-term and tourist rentals
detail: End false "short-term" contracts (*alquiler de temporada*) that landlords use to avoid the protections of a normal rental contract. Regulate short-term and tourist rentals so they do not take homes off the market. The programme has no rent limit.
c: Closing this gap is a simple change to the LAU, and many parties support it.
pos: It closes the gap that landlords use to avoid the rules that protect tenants.
neg: It becomes harder for students and workers sent from other places to find temporary housing.

title: Zero or very low VAT on basic food
detail: A wide VAT reform with zero or very low rates (*IVA superreducido*) on some basic foods (fish, meat and others) and on special products (for example for people with coeliac disease). Also a review of taxes on electricity, gas, fuel and public transport within EU rules.
c: 0% on basic food already applied in 2023 and 2024, and EU rules allow it. Shop prices fell by almost the full cut (Banco de España, CNMC). The Fedea think tank estimated that half of the savings went to the richest 40% of households. The wider review of taxes on energy and transport is harder, so we rate the whole promise B.
pos: Cheaper food, especially for poorer households.
neg: In 2023 half of the savings went to the richest 40% of households, according to Fedea. The state loses tax money.

s.t: Banco de España, Working Paper 2417 (2024): VAT cut pass-through to prices
CNMC, 10 Aug 2023: study of the VAT cut pass-through to food prices
Fedea (think tank), López Laborda et al., Apuntes 2023/02: who gained from the VAT cut

title: Cut the electricity tax to 0.5%
detail: Cut the special tax on electricity (*Impuesto Especial sobre la Electricidad*) to 0.5% for good, within EU limits.
c: The EU minimum is €0.5/MWh for businesses and €1/MWh for households. A 0.5% rate already applied from 2021 to 2023. It is realistic. In our estimate it costs about €1.5 billion a year.
pos: Cheaper electricity, and a reason to use electricity instead of gas or oil.
neg: The tax money it loses goes to the regions.

s.t: Directive 2003/96/EC on energy taxation: minimum €0.5/€1 per MWh (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Pensions that rise with prices; minimum pensions up step by step
detail: Raise pensions every year with consumer prices (*IPC*). Raise minimum pensions and pensions for people who did not pay enough social security (*pensión no contributiva*) "step by step", with a focus on the lowest incomes. No amounts are given.
c: The law already links pensions to consumer prices.
neg: Spending grows as the population gets older.

title: No cut for early retirement after 40 years of work
detail: End the pension cut for early retirement (*coeficiente reductor*) for people who paid social security for more than 40 years, and correct the cut for people who have already retired.
c: It is realistic. Doing it for people who have already retired costs more. Junts and Podemos want the same, so a majority is possible.
pos: People who have worked for 40 years or more can retire early without a cut.
neg: Higher spending, and it goes against the goal of people working longer.

title: A Basque minimum wage above the national one
detail: As part of a new political status, ask for full power to set a Basque minimum wage (*SMI*). It would match the cost of living, always be higher than the national minimum, and be agreed by unions and employers (*diálogo social*). No amount is given.
c: A separate minimum wage needs power over labour law (art. 149.1.7 of the Constitution). The "new political status" itself would need legal changes.

title: Protect and widen the Basque tax agreement (*Concierto Económico*)
detail: Change the *Concierto Económico* law to give the Basque Country more powers over money and taxes, and make sure state tax and budget reforms respect it. Also protect Navarre's *Convenio Económico*.
c: The *concierto* law changes by agreement in a joint commission. Widening it is realistic if the government needs PNV's votes.
pos: More tax powers for the Basque Country.
neg: It makes the conflict with other regions about sharing money between regions worse.
